### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s).

**41** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6073bb96b878eb2980724568ee526157b29ab141`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6073bb96b878eb2980724568ee526157b29ab141` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ea536dd70752bd4094c1d5ee25e4efc2e4d54d08` — the merge of head `22cc56d6c36b90821525ba353da6bcda7e76355b` into base `6073bb96b878eb2980724568ee526157b29ab141`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ea536dd70752bd4094c1d5ee25e4efc2e4d54d08 && git checkout ea536dd70752bd4094c1d5ee25e4efc2e4d54d08
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6073bb96b878eb2980724568ee526157b29ab141 22cc56d6c36b90821525ba353da6bcda7e76355b && git checkout -B drift-repro 6073bb96b878eb2980724568ee526157b29ab141 && git merge --no-ff 22cc56d6c36b90821525ba353da6bcda7e76355b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6073bb96b878eb2980724568ee526157b29ab141
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6073bb96b878eb2980724568ee526157b29ab141` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `22cc56d6c36b90821525ba353da6bcda7e76355b`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #20833 (body and its 3 comments: the dispatch claim, the dev report `5924706600`, the seat's ACCEPT `5924729189`), PR #21069 (body, 9-file list, net diff merge-base `d67b9428`..head: 9 files, +886/−31, equal to the PR's own totals), and the 33 check-runs on the head. Disclosure discipline held: classes and positions only; the read door outside the engine middleware chain is neither named nor described here.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The narrowing itself — right.** A data middleware registered `{ object: 'sys_activity' }` narrows `find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate` for any caller whose context is present and not `isSystem`: a system-context pre-scan of the parent pairs the caller's `where` would touch, one caller-scoped readability answer per parent object, then one `$or` branch per parent object (`object_name` + `record_id $in` the stored values) ANDed into `ctx.ast.where`. On the generic data doors that is the list, its `total`, the by-id read, the filtered query and the grouped count — the card's criterion for the engine-middleware doors, and the dogfood pin asserts it per returned row against the same door as the same member.
2. **One derivation — right.** `resolveReadableParentIds` is lifted out of `computeThreadVisibilityFilter` in `comment-access-hooks.ts` with its loop body intact: the same `withoutOperationPrivateKeys` envelope (the #7141 rule), the same `find(parent, { where: { id: { $in } }, fields: ['id'], limit: ids.length, context })`, the same catch-to-empty. The comment gate's thread assembly, verbatim `thread_id` filter and `READ_DENY_ALL` are unchanged, and both gates now call the one function. The comment gate's pins (`comment-access-hooks.test.ts`, `comment-read-visibility.test.ts`, `comments-permission-matrix.dogfood.test.ts`) are untouched by the diff and ran on the head (Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate).
3. **Fail-closed classes — right, and the same as the comment gate's.** Excluded for every non-system caller: a row whose parent the caller cannot read; a row whose parent no longer exists (the probe finds nothing — admins included, Q2); a row naming no parent, an object outside the machine-name shape, or an object the engine does not know (the probe throws → empty); a row naming `sys_activity` itself (no re-entry). A failing pre-scan → deny-all. A pre-scan at the 2,000-row bound → rows beyond it excluded, with the warning. `OBJECT_NAME_RE` equals the spec's `ObjectSchema.name` regex (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:1612`) and the comment parser's, so no legal object name is wrongly excluded. A platform object is a parent like any other: `sys_user` / `sys_member` / `sys_permission_set` / `sys_metadata` rows are kept exactly when the caller can read that record — card acceptance 1.
4. **Batching — right.** One caller-scoped read per parent OBJECT per request (sequential), plus one system pre-scan; never one per row. The integration pin counts exactly `[act_board:find, act_ledger:find]` for a list read.
5. **Not narrowed — right, same class as the comment gate.** System-context reads, context-less reads, and non-read operations pass through. Residual (not new): a context-less programmatic read on a bare kernel is unnarrowed by design; every transport carries a context.
6. **Public surface — unchanged; right.** `src/index.ts` is an explicit named barrel (no `export *`) and is not in the diff, so the new module-level exports (`resolveReadableParentIds`, `installActivityReadVisibility`, `parseActivityParent`, `ActivityParent`) are not package exports. `package.json` and `src/objects/**` are not in the diff. No accept set widens; one read's result set narrows.
7. **Wiring — right.** Installed inside the `kernel:ready` handler under its own `registerMiddleware` seam check, independent of the comment hooks' `registerHook` guard, with a loud warning when the seam is absent; a mount pin was added to `audit-plugin.test.ts`.
8. **`system-context.mdx` census row — right.** Row 45 now also anchors `activity-read-visibility.ts#installActivityReadVisibility` (the `ctx.context.isSystem` early return in the registered middleware closure, the one new elevation read), and the declared counts move by exactly that site: 107→108 sites, 113→114 property reads, 104→105 behaviour-bearing, 45→46 files, 90→91 symbols; packages stay 19 (plugin-audit was already counted). Folding into row 45 keeps the page's "rows 1–61 / 62–64" partition true; two-file anchor cells have precedent (rows 22, 49, 51, 58, 59). Judged green by `Lint & Repo Gates` on the head, which runs `check-system-context-census.mjs`.
9. **Scan window — right direction, residual stated.** The pre-scan carries the caller's `orderBy` but not its offset, so a caller paging past the 2,000th row in its own order loses rows (closed, warned) — the comment gate's bound, now on a table that grows per mutation. A timeline scoped by `object_name` + `record_id` never meets it.

Positions, not measured, same class as the comment gate and not this card's: (a) a `sys_activity` read now issues caller-scoped reads of parent objects, so an object opted into read audit may record probe reads; (b) field-level values inside a kept row (③ below).

### ② Semver level

- **Level — right.** `.changeset/20833-activity-parent-read-gate.md` grades `@objectstack/plugin-audit: minor`, the only package whose `src/**` moves. The act is a BREAKING runtime narrowing with no public-surface change: AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3 (`(narrowing)` is BREAKING) and the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major`; the WHICH-LEVEL ruling in `pr-automation.yml`, decision batch #35) carry breaking-ness by the BREAKING banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition, not by `major`, and ship it `minor`. `patch` would also have cleared the level axis (a `no` declaration stands it down) but would understate a declared BREAKING; `minor` is the convention's spelling.
- **BREAKING text — right.** The `**BREAKING**:` banner states what narrows and for whom. No FROM → TO mapping is owed: nothing an author can write is removed or renamed (barrel, `src/objects/**`, `package.json` unchanged), and the body says so.
- **ADR-0087 disposition — right.** Exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category in the gate's closed set, with its justification; the changeset body carries the same `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line the ADR-0087 reader takes the arm from.
- **`Clause-②:` line — right, and the reader accepts the shape.** PR body line 3 reads `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — an engine read …`. `readClause2Line` scans every body line (no line-1 requirement); `CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE` matches; the value token reads `no`; `readArmToken` reads `(narrowing)` from the remainder and does not look past the closing parenthesis, so the trailing prose is inert; `clause2LineDescribes` is false (the key appears once, no opening backtick). Declared, not malformed, not the `no (widening)` contradiction. `Check Changeset` on the head — the job that runs `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` against the merge base — is `success`.
- **Clause-②: no (narrowing)** matches the diff (no new key, export or accepted value; one read returns fewer rows) and is the line the dispatch order expected.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q1 — a read door outside the engine middleware chain.** Seat decision: a separate `security` family card at the seat's next filing window, direction as the dev recommends (serve such an object only through the engine path, or refuse the bypass for it; no per-object list, no second registration per gate); #20833 stays open. Verified here: PR line 1 is `Part of #20833`, no closing keyword in title or body, `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is `success`, so the cloud#2485 grant keyed on this card's merge commit stays withheld. Answered: the card's criterion is met on the engine-middleware doors this package can reach; the open door is outside this package and this PR and is escalated to that card, not a defect of this diff. Not named here.
- **Q2 — admins lose rows about a record that no longer exists.** Seat decision A, keep. Answered: right. It is the comment gate's existing rule for a deleted record's thread, so the one derivation stays one; a carve-out would need a per-object bypass member on `ISecurityService` (outside the file surface, `plugin-security` ⛔) with no measured pull; the deletion itself stays in `sys_audit_log`. Card acceptance 2 holds for every existing record, and the residual is stated in both the PR body and the changeset.
- **Q3 — deviations.** (1) `Part of` in place of the closing keyword: verified above, right. (2) No empty-branch probe push: process-only, no effect on the diff. (3) The `system-context.mdx` row: on the diff, required by the census gate, judged in ① item 8. (4) The revised admin pin case: the integration pin's admin is the caller the parent stand-in answers every record to, which models the measured service (no per-object bypass on `/auth/me/permissions`); the dogfood pin's admin reads both fixture records through the real door. Answered: accept all four.
- **Out-of-scope finding, the comment gate's same open door:** folded into the Q1 card by the seat. Answered: agree, same class, one close-out.
- **Out-of-scope finding, field-level values in a kept row** (a caller who can read the parent record but not every field sees the before/after values the row records; the writer masks credential fields only): outside this record-level gate's criterion and not blocking. Escalated: it is a data-exposure class with no carrier yet — the seat should give it a card or a row in the close-out rather than acceptance notes alone.
- **Dev "not measured" items** (multi-organization boot; `GET /search` said nothing; whole-repo build gates `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`, `check:i18n`, `skill-examples`; dogfood typecheck): the head's check-runs own these — see the gate line below. A multi-org boot stays unmeasured and is not this card's criterion.
- **Gate verdicts on the head** (the check-runs ARE the verdicts): 35 check-runs on `22cc56d6`, every one completed by 04:37Z — 33 `success`, 2 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`, the pin did not move; `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 `failure`. The ones this record leans on, each `success`: `Check Changeset` (the Clause-② line, the level axis, the ADR-0087 disposition, no-major); `Lint & Repo Gates` (the system-context census, the whole-repo lint the dev declared as a narrowing, and the `check:i18n` and `check:skill-examples` families the dev left NOT MEASURED); `Build Core` (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`); `Type Check · debt ledger` (`check:type-check-debt`); `Type Check · workspace`, `· source gates`, `· consumer gates` (the dogfood typecheck the dev could not run); `Test Core` 1/6–6/6 (the plugin-audit pins and the untouched comment-gate pins); `Dogfood Regression Gate` 1/3–3/3 (the new door pin and `comments-permission-matrix`); `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`; `Build Docs`; `Part-of PR must not also close its card`; `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`; `No other open PR may claim the same issue` and `… the same single-writer path`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`; `Spec property liveness`. So all four of the dev's NOT MEASURED gate families are answered green on the head.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20833-activity-parent-read-gate`
Reviewed-by: `session_01XY5uCwTjZj7884yYtyur4H`

**VERDICT: PASS**
